newsitem.title: USA: Nike says revenues up 50 pct in all regions.
newsitem.headline: Nike says revenues up 50 pct in all regions.

text.p: Nike Inc Chairman Phil Knight said revenues for the latest quarter were up more than 50 percent in each of its four global geographic regions.

"This is remarkably balanced growth for a company with trailing 12-month revenues approaching $9 billion," Knight said in a statement accompanying the company's results for its fiscal third quarter ending Feb. 28.
Nike's geographic sales regions include the U.S., Europe, Asia Pacific and Americas
The company's net income of $0.80 a share was well beyond average analyst expectations of $0.72, according to First Call.

Nike said U.S. footwear revenues were up 47 percent over last year's third quarter, bolstered by strong performance in key categories including men's basketball, women's fitness and men's running shoes.
Global apparel revenues grew 79 percent in the quarter on top of sharp increases a year earlier.

International athletic footwear and apparel revenues increased 67 percent to $982.9 million. Currency translations held down international revenue growth rates, the company said had the U.S. dollar remained constant at year-ago levels, international revenues would have increased 78 percent.

Sales were up over 100 percent on a constant-dollar basis in the company's two biggest overseas markets, Japan and Britain. Revenues were up 65 percent in Germany, 93 percent in Korea and 64 percent in Italy.

"In every market where Nike does business, futures orders were up double-digits on a constant-dollar basis," Knight said. "As a company, we're still in the nascent stages of our development outside the U.S., but this balanced growth of orders is testament to the emerging power of our brand globally."
U.S. athletic footwear and apparel revenues totaled $1.34 billion for the quarer, an increase of 51 percent over year-earlier levels.
Revenues from other Nike brands, which include Bauer, Cole Haan, Tetra Plastics and Sports Specialties, fell 3 percent to $102.3 million.
Consolidated gross margins for the quarter were 40.8 percent, up from 39.7 percent a year earlier. Selling and administrative expenses fell to 23.8 percent of revenues from 24.5 percent.
